test_description: Verify that computeFingerprint returns deterministic hashes regardless of object key insertion order in taskDef.checks and taskDef.inputs
test_assertions: computeFingerprint returns same hash for identical checks with different key insertion order
computeFingerprint returns same hash for identical inputs with different key insertion order
Deterministic hash survives across separate Node.js process invocations
change_description: Replace JSON.stringify with stableStringify in computeFingerprint for checks and inputs hashing, ensuring deterministic fingerprints regardless of key ordering
why_this_correction: Evidence from observe phase: helpers.ts:91 uses raw JSON.stringify for checks/inputs hashing, which serializes in insertion order only — no stable key ordering. Meanwhile hash/task.ts:42 already uses stableStringify (which sorts keys then recurses) for the same purpose. This inconsistency means semantically identical task definitions produce different fingerprints, breaking change detection, resume, retries, and caching. Replacing JSON.stringify with stableStringify makes the Fingerprint Determinism model enforceable.
